tempting.loose_reading: A skilled tradesperson is paired with something his trade cannot be carried on without.
tempting.why_wrong: A bookbinder works WITH an awl, a hand tool he holds to pierce the pages, just as a bootmaker works with a last, the wooden form he shapes the boot over; a caulker does not hold or handle a shipyard, he works AT it, so that pair is a worker and his workplace.

explanation: Relation: worker/tool. Just as a bookbinder uses an awl as a tool to punch sewing holes, a bootmaker uses a last, the foot-shaped form a boot is built on, as a tool.

distractor_rationales.reliquary is to bones: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a reliquary holds the bones of a saint), not worker/tool
distractor_rationales.tiff is to fracas: relation it instantiates instead: degree (a tiff is a petty quarrel, a fracas a noisy, rowdy one), not worker/tool
distractor_rationales.cassock is to serge: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (a cassock is made of serge), not worker/tool
distractor_rationales.caulker is to shipyard: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a caulker, who seals the seams of hulls, works in a shipyard), not worker/tool

tempting.loose_reading: The two abstract nouns name essentially the same thing, one a weightier-sounding word for the other.
tempting.why_wrong: Rancor and acrimony MEAN the same thing (bitter ill will), as lethargy and torpor both mean sluggish inactivity; perjury does not mean falsehood, it is one particular kind of falsehood, a lie told under oath, so that pair is category and member, not two words for one idea.

explanation: Relation: synonyms. Just as rancor and acrimony both mean bitter resentment, lethargy and torpor both mean sluggish, drowsy inactivity.

distractor_rationales.falsehood is to perjury: relation it instantiates instead: category/instance (perjury, a lie told under oath, is one kind of falsehood), not synonyms
distractor_rationales.humidor is to tobacco: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a humidor holds tobacco), not synonyms
distractor_rationales.armistice is to warfare: relation it instantiates instead: lack (an armistice is marked by having no warfare), not synonyms
distractor_rationales.friar is to friary: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a friar lives and works in a friary), not synonyms

tempting.loose_reading: The first is a ceremonial, emblem-like vessel or object traditionally associated with the second.
tempting.why_wrong: A cornucopia is a conventional emblem that stands for prosperity (it does not literally hold prosperity), as a phoenix stands for renewal; a chalice does not stand for a libation, it literally holds one, so the pair is a vessel and its contents, not a symbol and what it represents.

explanation: Relation: symbol/symbolized. Just as the cornucopia (the horn of plenty) is a conventional symbol of prosperity, the phoenix is a conventional symbol of renewal. The trap is the chalice: like the cornucopia it is a ceremonial vessel, but it physically holds the libation rather than standing for an idea.

distractor_rationales.chalice is to libation: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a chalice holds a libation, a ceremonial drink), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.ascetic is to indulgence: relation it instantiates instead: lack (an ascetic is characterised by having no indulgence), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.luthier is to gouge: relation it instantiates instead: worker/tool (a luthier carves instruments with a gouge), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.curate is to parish: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a curate works in a parish), not symbol/symbolized

tempting.loose_reading: The two words name closely related versions of one and the same idea.
tempting.why_wrong: The precise relation is that the first is a milder degree of the second: aversion is a milder abhorrence and a spat is a milder vendetta, but an acme is not a lesser zenith; the two words both mean the highest point and are equal in strength.

explanation: Relation: degree. Just as aversion is a milder form of abhorrence, a spat is a milder form of a vendetta.

distractor_rationales.blizzard is to whiteout: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (a blizzard causes a whiteout), not degree
distractor_rationales.coffer is to ducats: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a coffer holds ducats), not degree
distractor_rationales.acme is to zenith: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean the highest point), not degree
distractor_rationales.pestle is to pulverizing: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a pestle is used for pulverizing), not degree

tempting.loose_reading: The first names a condition of doing without, and the second names what that condition is about.
tempting.why_wrong: Anarchy is by definition a state that has no governance, just as an ingrate is a person who has no appreciation for kindness received; privation is not a state that has no impoverishment but means the same thing as impoverishment, so the pair are synonyms, not a bearer and what it lacks.

explanation: Relation: lack. Just as anarchy is characterised by having no governance, an ingrate is characterised by having no appreciation for what is done for him.

distractor_rationales.evergreen is to hemlock: relation it instantiates instead: category/instance (the hemlock tree is one kind of evergreen), not lack
distractor_rationales.millwright is to waterwheel: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a millwright builds a waterwheel), not lack
distractor_rationales.privation is to impoverishment: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (privation and impoverishment both mean a state of poverty and want), not lack
distractor_rationales.sexton is to graveyard: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a sexton works at the church graveyard, digging and tending graves), not lack

tempting.loose_reading: The second is the natural substance the first is built from or with.
tempting.why_wrong: A wigwam is MADE OF birchbark, as a cairn is made of fieldstone; a honeybee is not made of beeswax but produces it, so the pair is a creator and its creation, not an object and its material.

explanation: Relation: object/material. Just as a wigwam is made of birchbark, a cairn (a heap of stones marking a trail or grave) is made of fieldstone.

distractor_rationales.gaiety is to dejection: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (gaiety is the opposite of dejection), not object/material
distractor_rationales.pacifist is to belligerence: relation it instantiates instead: lack (a pacifist is characterised by having no belligerence), not object/material
distractor_rationales.honeybee is to beeswax: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a honeybee produces beeswax), not object/material
distractor_rationales.bellringer is to belfry: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a bellringer works in a belfry), not object/material

tempting.loose_reading: The first is a milder condition and the second is the extreme, overwhelming condition it can reach.
tempting.why_wrong: Disquiet is a milder degree of the same quality (fear) that horror is in its extreme form, as a glow is a milder degree of the brightness that incandescence is; overexertion is not a milder exhaustion but an excessive activity that produces exhaustion, so the relation is cause and effect, not degree.

explanation: Relation: degree. Just as disquiet is a mild form of fear and horror an intense one, a glow is a faint form of shining light and incandescence an intense, white-hot one.

distractor_rationales.bowyer is to longbow: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a bowyer makes longbows), not degree
distractor_rationales.overexertion is to exhaustion: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (overexertion brings on exhaustion), not degree
distractor_rationales.grapnel is to grappling: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a grapnel is used for grappling), not degree
distractor_rationales.tapster is to tavern: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a tapster draws drinks in a tavern), not degree

tempting.loose_reading: The first is a concrete thing that we connect with an abstract idea of decline and ruin, the second.
tempting.why_wrong: An orb is a conventional emblem that stands for a monarch's dominion, as a yoke is the conventional emblem of subjugation; termites do not stand for dilapidation by any convention, they literally cause it by eating timber, so the relation is cause and effect, not symbol.

explanation: Relation: symbol/symbolized. Just as the orb carried by a monarch is the traditional emblem of dominion, the yoke laid on a conquered people is the traditional emblem of subjugation.

distractor_rationales.termites is to dilapidation: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (termites cause the dilapidation of wooden structures), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.woodcarver is to altarpiece: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a woodcarver carves an altarpiece), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.gladness is to ecstasy: relation it instantiates instead: degree (gladness is a milder form of the joy that ecstasy is at its height), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.parboiling is to frying: relation it instantiates instead: preparation/act (potatoes are parboiled to prepare them for frying), not symbol/symbolized

tempting.loose_reading: The second is water that gathers in, or comes together with, the first.
tempting.why_wrong: A cistern is a vessel built to hold the runoff channelled into it from roofs, as a sachet is a small pouch made to hold lavender; a thaw holds nothing, it is an event that melts snow and so produces meltwater, so the relation is cause and effect, not container and contents.

explanation: Relation: container/contents. Just as a cistern is a tank that holds the runoff collected from a roof, a sachet is a small cloth pouch that holds dried lavender.

distractor_rationales.monotony is to variety: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (sameness is the opposite of variety), not container/contents
distractor_rationales.pinprick is to gash: relation it instantiates instead: degree (a pinprick is a tiny wound and a gash a deep one), not container/contents
distractor_rationales.searing is to braising: relation it instantiates instead: preparation/act (meat is seared to prepare it for braising), not container/contents
distractor_rationales.thaw is to meltwater: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (a thaw melts snow and ice and produces meltwater), not container/contents

tempting.loose_reading: x is a small hand implement and y is the -ing word that goes with it.
tempting.why_wrong: The precise relation is that x is the implement used to PERFORM the action y: a jimmy is used for prying, as a snuffer is used for dousing a candle flame; wadding is not an action a swab performs but the soft padding a swab is made of, so swab : wadding is object and material.

explanation: Relation: tool/function. Just as a jimmy (a short burglar's crowbar) is used for prying open doors and windows, a snuffer (a cup on a handle) is used for dousing candle flames.

distractor_rationales.flagon is to stout: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a flagon holds stout), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.swab is to wadding: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (a swab is made of wadding, soft cotton padding), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.loitering is to tarrying: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean lingering idly), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.distaste is to revulsion: relation it instantiates instead: degree (distaste is a milder form of revulsion), not tool/function

tempting.loose_reading: x is a skilled tradesperson and y is an object that comes out of, or is handled in, the practice of that trade.
tempting.why_wrong: The precise relation is that y is the finished work x produces: an embroiderer stitches a sampler, as a pamphleteer writes a tract; a farrier does not produce pincers but uses them as a tool to pull nails and old shoes from a hoof, so farrier : pincers is worker/tool.

explanation: Relation: creator/creation. Just as an embroiderer stitches a sampler (a piece of decorative needlework), a pamphleteer writes a tract (a short persuasive pamphlet).

distractor_rationales.spasm is to convulsion: relation it instantiates instead: degree (a spasm is a milder, more local form of a convulsion), not creator/creation
distractor_rationales.farrier is to pincers: relation it instantiates instead: worker/tool (a farrier works with pincers when shoeing horses), not creator/creation
distractor_rationales.prong is to trident: relation it instantiates instead: part/whole (a prong is one of the three points of a trident), not creator/creation
distractor_rationales.crossbones is to mortality: relation it instantiates instead: symbol/symbolized (the skull and crossbones carved on old gravestones conventionally stands for mortality), not creator/creation

tempting.loose_reading: x is what brings y into existence.
tempting.why_wrong: The precise relation is that x is an act or agent whose consequence is y, a resulting condition: arson results in a conflagration, as an allergen results in itchiness; a parodist is a person who deliberately composes a lampoon as a piece of writing, so parodist : lampoon is maker and made work (creator/creation), not a cause and the condition it produces.

explanation: Relation: cause/effect. Just as arson (deliberately setting fire to property) causes a conflagration (a large, destructive fire), an allergen causes itchiness in a sensitive person.

distractor_rationales.parodist is to lampoon: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a parodist writes a lampoon, a mocking satire), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.concierge is to hostelry: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a concierge works at a hostelry, an inn or hotel), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.tyro is to finesse: relation it instantiates instead: lack (a tyro, a raw beginner, has no finesse), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.guile is to artifice: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean crafty, cunning deceit), not cause/effect

tempting.loose_reading: x is what brings about y.
tempting.why_wrong: Oxidation is a natural process whose result is a patina, as an eruption is an event whose result is ashfall; a gimlet does not produce piercing as an outcome but is a hand tool a person uses to perform the action of piercing (boring) holes, so the pair is tool and the action it is used for, not cause and effect.

explanation: Relation: cause/effect. Just as oxidation causes a patina to form on metal, a volcanic eruption causes ashfall.

distractor_rationales.zeal is to fanaticism: relation it instantiates instead: degree (fanaticism is zeal carried to an extreme), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.hessian is to jute: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (hessian cloth is woven from jute), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.ankh is to immortality: relation it instantiates instead: symbol/symbolized (the ankh is the Egyptian symbol of eternal life), not cause/effect
distractor_rationales.gimlet is to piercing: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a gimlet is used for piercing small holes in wood), not cause/effect

tempting.loose_reading: The first stands for, or expresses, the second.
tempting.why_wrong: A weeping willow is a conventional emblem that stands for lamentation without being lamentation, as a dunce cap is an emblem of stupidity; contrition does not stand for penitence as an emblem, it is the same inward sorrow under another name, so the pair is synonyms.

explanation: Relation: symbol/symbolized. Just as the weeping willow is a conventional symbol of lamentation in funerary art, the dunce cap is a conventional symbol of stupidity.

distractor_rationales.contrition is to penitence: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean sincere sorrow for wrongdoing), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.topiarist is to secateurs: relation it instantiates instead: worker/tool (a topiarist shapes hedges with secateurs), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.pestilence is to depopulation: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (a pestilence causes depopulation), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.glassmaker is to glassworks: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a glassmaker works in a glassworks), not symbol/symbolized

tempting.loose_reading: x is an emblem or token conventionally bound up with y.
tempting.why_wrong: Rosemary stands for remembrance, an abstract idea it signifies; insignia does not stand for an epaulet, an epaulet is simply one member of the class of insignia (category/instance).

explanation: Relation: symbol/symbolized. Just as rosemary is the traditional emblem of remembrance, the beehive is the traditional emblem of industry (hard work).

distractor_rationales.insignia is to epaulet: relation it instantiates instead: category/instance (an epaulet is one kind of insignia), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.fuselage is to airliner: relation it instantiates instead: part/whole (the fuselage is the main body section of an airliner), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.tenderizing is to broiling: relation it instantiates instead: preparation/act (tenderizing meat is done to prepare it for broiling), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.rammer is to tamping: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a rammer is used for tamping (earth or gravel)), not symbol/symbolized

tempting.loose_reading: The second is a particular thing, here a seed, that is included within the broader first.
tempting.why_wrong: A peanut is one kind of legume, so the first names a class and the second one member of it, as a barnacle is one kind of crustacean; linseed is not a kind of putty but the seed whose oil glazier's putty is made with, so the pair is object and material.

explanation: Relation: category/instance. Just as a peanut is one kind of legume (not a true nut), a barnacle is one kind of crustacean (not a mollusk).

distractor_rationales.flippancy is to earnestness: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (flippancy, a joking lack of seriousness, is the opposite of earnestness), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.huntsman is to decoy: relation it instantiates instead: worker/tool (a huntsman uses a decoy to lure game birds), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.putty is to linseed: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (traditional putty is made with linseed oil), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.dramatist is to melodrama: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a dramatist writes a melodrama), not category/instance

tempting.loose_reading: x and y are two closely related words for the same kind of thing.
tempting.why_wrong: Unrest is a milder degree of insurrection, the same disorder at lower intensity; an amble is not a milder saunter, the two words name the same leisurely pace at the same intensity (synonyms).

explanation: Relation: degree. Just as unrest is a lesser degree of insurrection, a wavelet is a lesser degree of a billow (a great swelling wave).

distractor_rationales.twine is to sisal: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (twine is made of sisal fibre), not degree
distractor_rationales.amble is to saunter: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean an unhurried stroll), not degree
distractor_rationales.pollutant is to contamination: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (a pollutant causes contamination), not degree
distractor_rationales.forceps is to extracting: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (forceps are used for extracting (teeth)), not degree

tempting.loose_reading: The first is a kind of person who is the very opposite of what the second stands for.
tempting.why_wrong: A boor is by definition a person who has no tact, so the second word names the quality the first person is without; a dolt does not lack a savant, a savant is a second, opposite kind of person, so the pair is two opposites, whereas a heretic is by definition without orthodoxy.

explanation: Relation: lack. Just as a boor is characterised by having no tact, a heretic is characterised by having no orthodoxy.

distractor_rationales.frost is to wilting: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (a hard frost causes tender plants to wilt), not lack
distractor_rationales.dolt is to savant: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (a dolt, a stupid person, is the opposite of a savant, a learned one), not lack
distractor_rationales.musketeer is to ramrod: relation it instantiates instead: worker/tool (a musketeer loads with a ramrod), not lack
distractor_rationales.crowbar is to dislodging: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a crowbar is used for dislodging things wedged or nailed in place), not lack

tempting.loose_reading: The first is what you rely on to get the second done.
tempting.why_wrong: A splint is the implement that itself does the immobilizing, so the second word names the action the first object performs, as a mangle is the machine that does the wringing of wet laundry; cramming is not an implement and does not perform the examination, it is study done beforehand to get ready for it.

explanation: Relation: tool/function. Just as a splint is used for immobilizing a broken limb, a mangle (an old laundry wringer with rollers) is used for wringing water from washed clothes.

distractor_rationales.amity is to strife: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (amity, friendly peace, is the opposite of strife, bitter conflict), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.nonentity is to significance: relation it instantiates instead: lack (a nonentity is a person with no significance), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.drumhead is to calfskin: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (a traditional drumhead is made of calfskin), not tool/function
distractor_rationales.cramming is to examination: relation it instantiates instead: preparation/act (cramming is done to get ready for an examination), not tool/function

tempting.loose_reading: The first thing consists of the substance named second.
tempting.why_wrong: Polenta is made out of cornmeal, as a fiddlestring is made out of catgut: the second is the stuff the first is formed from; a blimp is not made of helium but is an envelope that is filled with helium (container/contents).

explanation: Relation: object/material. Just as polenta is made from cornmeal, a traditional fiddlestring is made from catgut.

distractor_rationales.recession is to joblessness: relation it instantiates instead: cause/effect (an economic recession leads to joblessness), not object/material
distractor_rationales.blimp is to helium: relation it instantiates instead: container/contents (a blimp's envelope holds helium), not object/material
distractor_rationales.respite is to lull: relation it instantiates instead: synonyms (both mean a temporary pause or break), not object/material
distractor_rationales.abacus is to computing: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (an abacus is used for computing sums), not object/material

tempting.loose_reading: The first is a single thing that stands for, or carries the meaning of, the larger idea named second.
tempting.why_wrong: Precisely, the first is a concrete emblem that by convention stands for the abstract idea named second (a pomegranate stands for fertility; a garland stands for glory); a tenet is not an emblem and stands for nothing - it is simply one of the beliefs that make up a creed, a part of the whole (part/whole).

explanation: Relation: symbol/symbolized. Just as the pomegranate is a traditional symbol of fertility, a garland (such as the victor's laurel garland) is a traditional symbol of glory.

distractor_rationales.constancy is to fickleness: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (constancy, steadfast loyalty, is the opposite of fickleness), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.lacemaker is to mantilla: relation it instantiates instead: creator/creation (a lacemaker makes a mantilla, a lace veil), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.tenet is to creed: relation it instantiates instead: part/whole (a tenet is one of the beliefs that make up a creed), not symbol/symbolized
distractor_rationales.publican is to alehouse: relation it instantiates instead: worker/workplace (a publican keeps and works in an alehouse), not symbol/symbolized

tempting.loose_reading: The two words name a thing and the stuff it is built up from.
tempting.why_wrong: A spearhead is made of the substance obsidian and a chessman is carved from the substance ebony; a strand is not made of cable, it is one component of a cable, so the pair is part to whole, not object to material.

explanation: Relation: object/material. Just as a spearhead can be chipped from obsidian, a chessman can be carved from ebony.

distractor_rationales.strand is to cable: relation it instantiates instead: part/whole (a strand is one of the twisted parts of a cable), not object/material
distractor_rationales.apogee is to perigee: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (an orbit's farthest point and its nearest point), not object/material
distractor_rationales.peacock is to ostentation: relation it instantiates instead: symbol/symbolized (the peacock conventionally stands for ostentation), not object/material
distractor_rationales.fueling is to takeoff: relation it instantiates instead: preparation/act (an aircraft is fueled to make ready for takeoff), not object/material

tempting.loose_reading: The second word names a particular named variety that goes with the more general first word.
tempting.why_wrong: A cockle is one kind of bivalve and an oleander is one kind of shrub; jasper is not a kind of amulet, it is the stone an amulet can be carved from, so the pair is object to material, not category to instance.

explanation: Relation: category/instance. Just as a cockle is a kind of bivalve, an oleander is a kind of shrub.

distractor_rationales.amulet is to jasper: relation it instantiates instead: object/material (an amulet can be carved from jasper, a stone), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.benediction is to curse: relation it instantiates instead: antonyms (a spoken blessing and its opposite, a spoken curse), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.snack is to repast: relation it instantiates instead: degree (a snack is a lesser, lighter version of a meal), not category/instance
distractor_rationales.auger is to unclogging: relation it instantiates instead: tool/function (a plumber's auger is used for unclogging drains), not category/instance
